diagrams.title: The Buy-Low, Sell-High Flip Loop
diagrams.subtitle: Register cheap, screen hard, price on comps, list wide, renew with intent

stages.label: Register Cheap, Cap the Spend
stages.detail: Registrations cluster around $6 to $10 with $20 to $50 per-name caps; .com first, since about 75% of all domain sales are .com (Thinking Blueprint), with .ai and .io as the hot alternates.

stages.label: Reject Flawed Candidates
stages.detail: Any candidate with a dash, a creative misspelling, or a date is rejected before it reaches the cart (Make Money with Stacy La).

stages.label: Price on Appraisal Plus Comps
stages.detail: Pair the GoDaddy appraisal with NameBio comparable sales, and relist at a new price if 90 days pass without a sale (David Utke).

stages.label: List Wide on Afternic
stages.detail: Point a Namecheap-registered name's nameservers to Afternic to cut the commission from 25% to 15% and unlock fast transfer plus a for-sale lander (David Utke).

stages.label: Close in Escrow, Renew or Drop
stages.detail: Refuse pay-later buyers and close only through escrow (DomainRacer Hindi); auto-renew keepers and drop unsold dead weight before renewal (Andrey Verevko).

diagrams.caption: KT Blogger turned a fresh $10 hand-registration into a $1,500 sale, while Andrey Verevko bought at $10, renewed at 15, sold at 20, and ended five bucks in the hole.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Step order follows the loop described across sixteen Q1 operators; all prices and commission rates are as stated by the named practitioners, not independently verified.
diagrams.note: Sources Thinking Blueprint (12ohlClK0g8 @ 00:02:27), Make Money with Stacy La (SuiwtFN2AO8 @ 00:04:48), David Utke (A6-lVEeaHEs @ 00:05:02 and 00:10:27), DomainRacer Hindi (eDmh_k07UEg @ 00:03:18), Andrey Verevko (bVQnMN-Qrd8 @ 00:09:05).

stages.detail: Lower bound of the 30-50% liquid-name band.

stages.detail: The bid Rosener reported for Diagnose.com at Media Options.

stages.label: Illiquid-Name Buy Ceiling
stages.detail: Rosener's cap for illiquid names, set because only about 10% of a portfolio sells in a lifetime.

diagrams.caption: Profit is set on the buy. Rosener pays at most 10% of expected resale for illiquid names and 30-50% for liquid ones, and bid about $30-35K on a $100-150K retail name.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The $75K, $45K and $15K stages are arithmetic, applying Rosener's stated percentages to the $150K top of his Diagnose.com range; the retail range and the $30-35K bid are his reported figures.
diagrams.note: Sources domainsherpa Valuation Room with Drew Rosener (KZqosumnXfg @ 01:09:57) and the 10x ask rule (cb-n0okmiuw @ 00:17:23).

diagrams.title: GoDaddy Closeout Buy-Now Price Decay
diagrams.subtitle: How the 5-day declining Closeout bottoms at $5
diagrams.caption: GoDaddy's Closeout buy-now starts at $11, drops $1 a day, then sits at $5 on the final day, after the 10-day auction that opens on day 26 of the expiry cycle.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Daily steps assume the 5-day Closeout window starting day 36 as mapped by the GoDaddy panel; the $3 final-day drop is the gap between the day 4 price and the stated $5 floor.
diagrams.note: Sources GoDaddy (0f-o9p0h6u8 @ 00:09:23) for the closeout pricing and GoDaddy (OM_5VESPepY @ 00:22:17) for the drop-cycle timing.

diagrams.title: .com Pricing Across Dedicated Registrars
diagrams.subtitle: Price every name on its renewal rate, not first-year bait
diagrams.caption: The cheapest published .com figures sit within about three dollars of each other, while a 1-cent host offer that secretly charges $40 shows why renewal price decides.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Typical values use the renewal or at-cost figure where a register-versus-renew split was reported; prices are as quoted by each practitioner at recording time.
diagrams.note: Sources Design Guy (mMGvtO-bkPI @ 00:00:59), SEARCHLIGHT HQ (RClpPcLHviU @ 00:00:30), David Utke (UkMYRY9wDN0 @ 00:10:42), Create a Pro Website (08Ekqe45IH0 @ 00:00:14).

diagrams.title: Exact-Match Domain Acquisition Gates
diagrams.subtitle: Volume, intent, footprint and deal readiness before the bid

nodes.question: Does the exact phrase draw more than 1,000 exact-match searches per month?
nodes.fail_action: Drop traffic-based valuation and price through buyer type, equity and industry trend phase (Chris Zuiker).

nodes.question: Do the live Google results confirm the right booking or research intent?
nodes.fail_action: Put the money toward building a better website instead (Launch with Bryan).

nodes.question: Is the name a standalone asset rather than part of a same-day EMD batch?
nodes.fail_action: Abort the batch; 22 sites with 19 registered within 35 seconds reads as doorway abuse (LLMrefs AI SEO).

nodes.question: Are financing and a fill-in-the-number contract ready before the approach?
nodes.pass_next: Acquire, expecting any buy above $100K to get shopped around
nodes.fail_action: Stage funds, paperwork and a broker first, or bridge the gap with an option-plus-lease carrying a $25-50K deposit on a $500K name (Rosener).

diagrams.caption: Rosener values generic .coms from exact-match volume above 1,000 monthly searches and an 85% top-organic click share; Gargiulo paid $1M for vpn.com after nearly 4 years.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Gate order is an organizing sequence across Q5 practitioners; whether EMDs still carry SEO benefit is disputed, with PPC Better saying none since 2012.
diagrams.note: Sources domainsherpa with Andrew Rosener (HfWOYwPZ1HU @ 00:11:38), Launch with Bryan (ASaM7hIMKVI @ 00:03:28), LLMrefs AI SEO (XEh3aA3iqtI @ 00:00:55), VPN.com (nwlWrMSMdUU @ 00:01:14), domainsherpa with Michael Gargiulo (J6_UP-VNOco @ 00:31:50).

diagrams.title: Trademark and Dispute Defense Around the Portfolio
diagrams.subtitle: Screen before the buy, answer every complaint, read registry terms

center.focus: Hold generic and brandable names without inviting UDRP filings

spokes.kpi: Google search, EU trademark and design view, and WIPO global brands database cleared, with no term tied to one major company (live NDDCamp)
A response filed on every complaint; kerosoft.co was lost by default to a $1,330 Forum filing (live NDDCamp, Steven Rinehart)
Terms read before buying, including .si moral type clauses and Afnic's two-week reply deadline (domainsherpa)
String run through the Name Collision Observatory early, never relied on alone (ICANN)

diagrams.caption: A typical UDRP lands in about 60 days versus 259 for an ACPA final judgment, and a complainant's run costs about $5,000 in lawyer fees plus a $1,500 filing fee.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Timelines and costs are as reported by Doug Isenberg and NDDCamp panelists; Steven Rinehart separately quotes 34 to 44 days for a UDRP.
diagrams.note: Sources GigaLaw with Doug Isenberg (GI9Us2WWsAo @ 00:06:31), live NDDCamp (PdwE4T9wmMo @ 00:04:24 and 00:33:12), Steven Rinehart (BL9pY270FpM @ 00:02:37), domainsherpa (4lvZ-LZJ3Sc @ 00:19:19), ICANN (ubAwLfPKk6s @ 00:02:48).

diagrams.title: First-Month Portfolio Roadmap
diagrams.subtitle: Capital, cheap sourcing, theme gating and a capped listing engine

weeks.title: Fund the Ledger and Model the Bad Year
weeks.deliverable: Starting capital set on the GoDaddy Domain Academy $500 challenge model, with a downside case built from three sales totaling $9.4K that left $900 profit before a $4K trademark dispute (Ownerly)
weeks.gate: Generic terms only, since trademark terms invite UDRP filings (POWERS Pod)

weeks.title: Source Closeouts Every Day
weeks.deliverable: Mid-day searches of $1-$50 GoDaddy closeouts (Mike Zigger) and about $5 Dynadot closeouts versus $10-20 elsewhere (Chris Koerner)
weeks.gate: Registrar appraisals ignored as an anchor; Koerner has seen names sell 99% below Dynadot's appraisal

weeks.title: Gate Hand-Registration Themes
weeks.deliverable: 365 days of exact-match godaddy.com search history pulled through Afternic for each theme (Andrew Allemann)
weeks.gate: Pause any theme where 50 names show no searches

weeks.title: List, Lease, and Cap Every Bid
weeks.deliverable: Afternic listings, the venue for 21 of Allemann's 25 sales, plus lease terms at 0.5-1 point per month with a 5-10% option fee (Rosener on Tim Ferriss)
weeks.gate: Late-bidding bot whose max bid cannot be raised later, and a renewal ceiling priced against cash after $100K into 260-270 names met three dry months

diagrams.caption: Annual sell-through runs roughly 1-3% of a portfolio, so one or two names carry the year; Allemann logged 8 of 25 sales as lease-to-own deals.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The four-week sequence is an organizing frame; the practitioners did not prescribe a weekly schedule, and all dollar and rate figures are as they reported them.
diagrams.note: Sources Ownerly (xPtTNJU_OGE @ 00:17:49), POWERS Pod (S9SNhuYObsA @ 00:30:09), GoDaddy Domain Academy (d1VjM9-Tyig @ 00:41:30), Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast (aba_NmtzK1I @ 00:08:07), Andrew Allemann (E4jnQONuo6E @ 00:24:00), Tim Ferriss (ApCGeST90RA @ 01:03:55).
